headline: High risk from shared filesystem and broad egress: transformers can write/read files and xonsh can execute those outputs as shell input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: transformers can read/write filesystem and emit files or stdout, while xonsh consumes shell commands and Python expressions from stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if xonsh ingests transformer-generated text as commands. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF xonsh reads transformer-produced stdout or files as executable shell input
IF the operator copies model output into xonsh without sanitization
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter and manual review before pasting output into xonsh
Disable automatic execution of generated shell snippets
Route transformer output to a plain-text file, not stdin
Add a prompt-injection filter for any text passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read access, so any shared workspace can expose text, source code, configuration, or environment variables from xonsh to transformers or vice versa. No secrets-handling or isolation boundary is documented between them, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted directory
IF either agent is given sensitive files or environment variables
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict sensitive files with OS permissions
Avoid placing secrets in shared directories
Turn off network egress for the agent handling sensitive data
Review outputs before exporting them outside the host

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells, and transformers also supports multiple instances while xonsh does not. If they target the same directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite each other's outputs. Because no locking or coordination is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF their outputs are produced concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Use read-only mounts for one agent
Checkpoint files before each write
Avoid shared git state unless one agent is read-only

D_cascading_error.rationale: transformers can generate text, code, or summaries that xonsh may then execute or use in shell workflows. That makes A's output a likely input to B without a built-in verification step. The interaction is inferred from documented I/O surfaces, not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes transformer output as commands or notebook cells
IF no human or automated verification step checks the generated text
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require human approval for any executable output
Convert A's output to data-only formats
Log and diff B's inputs before execution
Reject outputs containing shell metacharacters unless reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no handled secrets or special regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch shown. The only plausible issue is operational logging or retention if the operator feeds regulated data into either agent, which is outside the documented defaults.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workspace
IF the deployment adds logging or retention policies not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings before deployment
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
Review logs for accidental sensitive-data capture
